text: [intrigued] This piece of paper might be the only time aliens ever called Earth. [pause] August, 1977. A radio telescope in Ohio is listening for aliens. Late one night, it hears something so loud... the computer runs out of numbers, and switches to letters. [slowly] Six. E. Q. U. J. Five. [pause] It rises, peaks, and fades in seventy-two seconds, exactly like a signal from deep space. On the exact frequency scientists had guessed aliens would use. [pause] Days later, astronomer Jerry Ehman finds it. He circles it in red... and writes one word. [long pause] Telescopes have searched that spot for decades. [whispers] It never came back. [pause] And the telescope that heard it? [deadpan] Torn down in 1998... to expand a golf course. [pause] In 2024, scientists suggested a natural flash, in a cloud of hydrogen. But nobody can prove it. [pause] So all we have... is this piece of paper.
